summary: Introductory reliability intake for Zenovate's AI inference platform evaluation. Focus on multi-region failover, partial-degradation modes, regional routing preferences, and SLAs. Customer seeks guidance on tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated vs private with emphasis on data residency and auditability.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-09 09:34 PDT (58 minutes)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Kim (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Zenovate - Head of Platform), Anjali Rao (Zenovate - SRE), Diego Morales (Zenovate - CTO)

[00:00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, yeah, uh quick round of intros and then we'll dig into how you think about reliability and failure modes.
[00:00:12] Marcus Li: good morning, thanks samir. i'm Marcus, i run platform at Zenovate. We're evaluating inference setups, mainly leaning hosted-first but we need strong failover and we have some strict data residency rules.
[00:00:25] Leah Kim: great, thanks Marcus. can you say a bit about scale and traffic patterns? bursty, steady, percent p50/p95 latency goals?
[00:00:35] Marcus Li: yeah so our peak is about 120 reqs/s across EU and NA during trading hours, bursty on market open. p95 latency target is sub 350ms for the high-quality risk model, but we can accept a degraded path at p95 ~600ms if it keeps service alive.
[00:00:50] Anjali Rao: also we need audit logs for every inference for compliance, and any data staying in-region for EU customers.
[00:00:58] Leah Kim: ok, got it. quick outline — i'll run through Redwood's routing and fallback primitives, talk dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and then we can map to your SLOs.

[00:01:12] Leah Kim: first, multi-region routing. Redwood supports region-aware routing with weighted traffic splits, geo-preference, and automatic failover. The routing plane can do active-active or active-passive. In active-active we route to the closest healthy region; in active-passive you keep a warm standby region that you fail over to.
[00:01:30] Diego Morales: how warm is warm? like do you maintain model state and KV cache? We have large KV caches for session context.
[00:01:40] Leah Kim: good question. for hosted we maintain optional cross-region prefix caching plus per-region KV cache. Warm standby means we keep model shards loaded and a minimal warmed pool — not the full production pool unless you opt into reserved capacity. For Dedicated you can configure hot-standby GPUs in the standby region but that costs more.
[00:01:58] Marcus Li: okay so if NA hits a problem we fail to EU — but do we lose session context?
[00:02:06] Leah Kim: by default yes you lose ephemeral KV unless you replicate KV state. We have an asynchronous KV replication option, but it's eventual. For strict session continuity you'd want either a single-region private deployment or a dedicated cross-region replication strategy.
[00:02:20] Anjali Rao: is the replication managed by Redwood or do we have to pipe our traces? Concerned about PII getting replicated inadvertently.
[00:02:30] Leah Kim: replication is a Redwood-managed feature but you can enable field-level redaction and KMS controls. For EU-only data residency we can set policies so certain customer IDs never leave EU.

[00:02:42] [00:02:44] Samir Patel: one more primitive — partial degradation. We can define a fallback policy that when latency or error rate crosses thresholds we switch to cheaper model variants or reduced response size. For example, switch from risk-model-3b to risk-model-1b or to a cached summary path.
[00:03:00] Marcus Li: Hmm, switching to a 1b sounds like a big quality hit. How do you measure or guard against bad regresses?
[00:03:08] Leah Kim: we attach eval sets to rollout policies. you can set quality gates — if the fallback policy causes metric regressions beyond an allowed delta we won't auto-fallback, only manual. Also we support canary ring rollouts and A/B to validate.
[00:03:22] Diego Morales: can we do hybrid — like a hedged request where we send to both variants and take first response? Concerned about cost.
[00:03:30] Leah Kim: hedging is supported but it's costlier. We can do smart hedging: hedge only for top percentile requests or during incident windows. Redwood Optimize can recommend which paths to hedge to meet SLO with minimal cost.

[00:03:45] Anjali Rao: about SLA — what does Redwood guarantee for hosted?
[00:03:49] Samir Patel: our hosted SLA for availability is 99.9% for paid tiers with documented latency SLOs per model. For Dedicated we offer contractual SLAs with tighter availability and performance windows. Private deployments are negotiated as part of enterprise contract.
[00:04:03] Marcus Li: what's included in the SLA — is failover time specified?
[00:04:07] Samir Patel: failover is characterized — we provide mean time to failover estimates for different topologies. For active-active it's usually seconds to tens of seconds depending on DNS and client re-routing; for active-passive with warm standby we target under 2 minutes for capacity spin-up, but that depends on whether you have reserved hot standby.
[00:04:24] Marcus Li: that variability is tricky for our SREs. We need deterministic worst-case for compliance audits.
[00:04:30] Leah Kim: then Dedicated with reserved cross-region hot-standby is the safest. You pay for reserved capacity but we can guarantee cold-starts don't exceed a bounded time because the standby remains warm.

[00:04:42] [00:04:45] Diego Morales: what about telemetry — we need per-token latency, token-level cost, and traceability to requests, and of course audit logs with immutable storage.
[00:04:55] Samir Patel: Redwood Console exposes token-level accounting, per-route traces, and immutable audit exports to your S3 bucket. For Private we ship logs into your KMS-backed bucket and can integrate with your SIEM.
[00:05:10] Anjali Rao: does the audit record include model prompt and response?
[00:05:14] Leah Kim: by default we redact PII fields on export if you enable redaction rules. You can configure full verbose exports for internal audits, but for compliance we often recommend hashed or tokenized prompt storage.

[00:05:25] Marcus Li: in the worst case where region is down and we fallback to a smaller model, our business wants an explicit indicator in responses so downstream systems know this was degraded. Is that supported?
[00:05:35] Leah Kim: yes, you can add structured metadata to responses, e.g., "x-redwood-degradation: model=1b, fallback=true, fallback_reason=latency_spike" so downstream services can adjust.

[00:05:46] [00:05:50] Diego Morales: network partitions at cloud provider level — can Redwood chain fallback across providers? like fail to GCP from AWS?
[00:05:58] Leah Kim: Redwood Hosted spans multiple cloud regions/providers and we can route across providers, but private deployments are constrained to your network. Cross-cloud failover needs config for data egress rules — for EU residency you may want provider-specific policies.

[00:06:12] Marcus Li: can we set per-customer routing — EU customers always stay in EU even if NA is healthy?
[00:06:18] Samir Patel: yes, we support per-customer routing policies and can enforce region locks for specific tenant IDs.

[00:06:24] Anjali Rao: about incident runbooks — do you provide playbooks or runbooks for SLO breaches?
[00:06:30] Leah Kim: yes, Redwood ships operational playbooks: detection thresholds, circuit-breaker settings, automatic retries with jitter, when to enable fallback paths, and escalation contacts. We can also co-author runbooks for your ops team during pilot.

[00:06:44] [00:06:47] Marcus Li: what's the instrumentation overhead for continuous batching and KV cache — does that add latency variability?
[00:06:54] Leah Kim: continuous batching optimizes throughput; for low-latency p95 it will dispatch smaller batches when latency budgets are tight. There's a tradeoff: smaller batches increase per-token compute; continuous batching is adaptive. You can pin strict latency profiles so the runtime prioritizes latency over token cost.

[00:07:09] Diego Morales: curious about circuit breakers — does Redwood allow a manual override to flip to full degrade mode?
[00:07:15] Leah Kim: yes, you can have manual escalation via Console or API to flip policies, lock a model version, or force routing to a specific region.

[00:07:24] Anjali Rao: security — KMS integration for key management? HSM? and SOC2 cert?
[00:07:30] Samir Patel: we integrate with major KMS providers and offer customer-managed keys for Private. We also support HSM-backed key stores in Dedicated/Private. Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant — we'll send the attestation.

[00:07:42] Marcus Li: about cost — if we do reserved hot-standby in EU and NA is active, how should we think about unit economics?
[00:07:50] Leah Kim: reserved capacity is priced as a commit for GPU pools; hot-standby adds a fraction of that cost. Redwood Optimize can run a cost-sensitivity analysis given your traffic profile; often the delta for guaranteed failover is 20-40% overhead versus pure hosted burst.

[00:08:06] [00:08:10] Diego Morales: can we test this without a big integration? like a smoke test?
[00:08:15] Samir Patel: yes, proposal is a 2-week hosted pilot with a skinned plan — we perform a baseline run using your traffic trace, run failover simulation (we'll induce a region outage in staging), and measure degradation impact.

[00:08:28] Marcus Li: timeline — we need vendor decision by end of June for Q3 rollout. Is that feasible?
[00:08:34] Samir Patel: yes, pilot in May, analysis early June, then contract.

[00:08:40] Leah Kim: last notes — regarding privacy we can configure selective replication, redaction, and field-level encryption. For session continuity across regions we recommend rehydration strategies and maybe streaming checkpoints.

[00:08:55] [00:09:00] Anjali Rao: can you send the playbook and a sample pilot config?
[00:09:03] Samir Patel: yes we'll attach those.

[00:09:05] Diego Morales: and a cost table for hot-standby vs on-demand?
[00:09:08] Leah Kim: yes, Leah will prepare the cost estimate.

[00:09:12] Samir Patel: cool, let's recap. we'll send SOC2 + security, pilot template + cost, and Leah will schedule baseline with Marcus for next week. any other blockers?
[00:09:22] Marcus Li: none from me. thanks.
[00:09:25] Anjali Rao: thanks all.

[00:09:28] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'Redwood Dedicate' appears once, 'privet' instead of 'private' in one spot. Some speaker labels are informal.
